title: Special Topics in Religious Studies; Sacred and Desecrated: Archaeology and the Destruction of Heritage Sites
description: Sacredness is the first human idea to find expression in the material world. From prehistoric burials and cave paintings to today's temples, churches, and mosques; sacred places have deep connections to the communities that created them. They also have similarly profound negative associations for people who feel excluded or outraged by their existence. Both willful destruction and neglect have devastated many religious sites for that reason. This course examines historical and modern desecrations in the Middle East in terms of their causes and effects.
